newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot posts record earnings, sees 'strong' year.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot posts record earnings, sees 'strong' year.

text.p: Home Depot Inc., the nation's largest home improvement retailer, reported record earnings for the latest quarter Tuesday and said it was looking forward to strong earnings for the coming year.

The company said it earned $251.1 million, or 52 cents a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Feb. 2 compared with year-earlier earnings of $185.3 million, or 39 cents a share. Sales jumped 32 percent to $5.0 billion from $3.8 billion.
For the year, Home Depot said it earned $937.8 million, or $1.94 a share, on sales of $19.5 billion against year earlier profits of $731.5 million, or $1.54 a share, on sales of $15.4 billion.

"We are extremely happy with the results for the quarter and fiscal year, and we look forward to another year of strong earnings growth in fiscal 1997," said Bernard Marcus, chairman and chief executive officer.

Home Depot said it continued to expand, adding 33 new stores and relocating two stores in the fourth quarter, bringing the total to 512 stores, including 483 Home Depot stores and 5 EXPO Design Centres in the United States and 24 Home Depot stores in Canada.
Home Depot's stock was up $1.625 to $53.875 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
